reason: Quote is verbatim and the list was unvalidated on 13 Aug, but it was a loose 'if we need to change' remark, not an agreed step. The 11 Sep sync (L2525) decided the CMS trusts Salesforce completely: operator/partner IDs go in the deal payload and the CMS provisions or overwrites from it. This removes most of the dual-system ID reconciliation risk. WAGR-20 (brand-to-Operator derivation, 100% reconciliation dry-run), WAGR-470 (migration scope) and WAGR-489 (ID protection) partly cover the rest. What is left is a small gap: no explicit step to confirm the final active operator/partner list before production.
q1: found. All four quote segments are present verbatim (whitespace-normalised) in the re-fetched doc 1jcr9oC55uUZqovDGyI_odU0PSFQdavpADjF3c_R443s at line 1223 onward, timestamp ~01:06:40. Speakers are correct (Emily Vandenberg, Kobi Kunasekaran). The L1271 (24 Jul) quote was not re-fetched; it is background only.
q2: partially supports. Emily: 'we haven't really validated that list'. Kobi: 'if we need to change those IDs before we go into production, we just have to make sure we change it on both systems'. Joyce then says 'There's nothing wrong with the ID naming conventions... we might not need specific operators to be in the system period... or we might just need to change the status'. Kobi: 'we can always update later... lists are from whatever was in Air Table... some of them are probably not active'. It is a conditional reassurance and an informal acknowledgement. No one asked for or agreed a pre-production validation step. The claim's 'must be changed in both before production' overstates it. Joyce's concern is about which operators exist and their status, not about the IDs, and operator/partner status is automated from active deals (L1784, L1828).
q3: Yes, a later meeting weakens it. L1902 and L1904 (18 Aug): Strahinja accepts the ID sheet, which is a sandbox starting point. L2525 (11 Sep, doc 1JrZTaJQB49Swpnz3SjTb-o-E28mRHEmGWaQCU-TMm5c, 00:48:08) decided: no new endpoint, operator and partner with their IDs go in the deal message, the CMS 'trust[s] Salesforce completely' and overwrites existing data, and the unknown operator/partner error is crossed out. Salesforce is now the single source for operator/partner identity, so manual two-system reconciliation of IDs is largely moot. L2104 and L2299: current sandbox data is not production, and a clean production import is planned. L3226 (28 Sep): data import templates and cleanup are now urgent. These cover migration in general, not the operator list specifically.
q4: Partly covered. WAGR-460 (Requirements, unassigned, 0 comments) covers the Deal ID to CMS row map before cutover. It also lists 'WagerTech completes any manual Operator/Partner CMS mappings' under hypercare, which looks stale against L2525. WAGR-100 (Jumpr Review, Cedrick, 1 comment) auto-generates the IDs and confirms all 63 current values match the derivation, so the format is validated, but whether each record is active is not. WAGR-20 (Ready, unassigned, 1 comment) production migration plan includes 'brand-to-Operator derivation with alias entries' and a dry-run reconciliation of 100% of source rows, so the claim's statement that WAGR-20 does not cover operators/partners is inaccurate for operators. WAGR-489 (Requirements) protects Operator/Partner IDs after first activation. WAGR-470 (Open, Kobi) covers the historical migration scope decision. WAGR-245 (Airtable data-quality C1-C9) was closed 10 Aug as 'will revisit'. No ticket explicitly says 'WagerTech confirms the authoritative active operator/partner list before production'. JQL searches run: text ~ 'operator list' / 'Airtable' / 'Operator_External_ID__c' / 'unknown_operator' (broad results, relevant: WAGR-489, 470, 460, 245, 320, 100), and text ~ 'Partner_External_ID__c' / 'operator partner list' / 'reconcile' (relevant: WAGR-460, 489, 100, 131, 463).
corrections: what_differs overstates the meeting: Kobi said 'if we need to change', which is not an agreed requirement to change IDs in both systems.
WAGR-20 does cover operator derivation (brand-to-Operator with alias entries, plus a reconciliation dry-run). Partners are not named explicitly.
Add L2525 (2026-09-11): the CMS trusts Salesforce and provisions/overwrites operators/partners from the deal payload. This is the main later evidence, and the variance omits it.

WAGR-460's hypercare line about manual Operator/Partner CMS mappings and WAGR-100's out-of-scope note about unknown_operator look stale against L2525. A better action is to refresh WAGR-460 and add an active-list confirmation line to WAGR-20.
